reuse.why: Every expected-amount computation (server, preview, API model, client views and editor) goes through the existing getScheduledAmount, and the approximate tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: No copy of the rule is added; the old rangeRounding variation is removed instead of kept beside the new rule.

placement.why: The rule stays in shared/schedules.ts, the API field is computed in the scheduleModel mapper and typed in api-handlers, matching the tree's layers.

scope.why: Focused on the rule and the API field; touching every client caller is needed for the new op argument, but the step-1 release note now describes a rule that step 4 replaced.

maintainability.why: A single function with a required op parameter makes every caller state its operator, so future rule changes are made in one place.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All 14 call sites use getScheduledAmount; no inline amount computation remains.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the tolerance is taken from getApproxNumberThreshold rather than re-derived.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts gains a required op parameter (replacing the removed rangeRounding option) and one isapprox branch that the request introduces; every call site, including schedule-template and api-models, passes its operator.
